display.title: Episode 469: Saved by a Miracle, Chapter 1
display.summary_short: A week after Purim, Uncle Yossi explains why the Megillah calls us Yehudim, and a story begins: a Chassid framed for theft is told by the Alter Rebbe to come back next week, after his court date.
display.summary_long: Broadcast one week after Purim 5751. Uncle Yossi asks what message should stay with us from Purim. In the Megillah the Jewish people are called Yehudim, a name linked to 'modeh', to thank and to admit, as in Modeh Ani and Modim: we thank Hashem and acknowledge that He alone is G-d. The Sages teach that whoever rejects idol worship is called a Yehudi, like Mordechai, who refused to bow to Haman. He prays to see the greatest miracle, Hashem's return to Tzion with Moshiach. After the Hakochainik march, a yeshiva student leads the Shema and everyone gives tzedakah. Story time begins the story Uncle Yossi calls 'Through the Eyes of a Tzaddik'. Reb Baruch, an honest supervisor at a government lumberyard in a Russian town, is admired by the local minister. A jealous, cruel man named Alex hides twenty costly railroad logs in Reb Baruch's barn and accuses him of theft. Summoned to the minister's office on Tuesday, Reb Baruch goes to the Alter Rebbe, who smiles and tells him to come back next Sunday. Trusting the tzaddik, he decides not to appear. What happens next is left for next week.
display.lesson: We are called Yehudim because we thank Hashem and acknowledge Him alone; and trust in Hashem and in the guidance of a tzaddik gives courage.
